game.title: Dice sum
game.description:
Two dice are rolled independently. Repeated numbers are separate faces.
- Die 1 (8 faces, each equally likely): 6, 6, 7, 7, 12, 12, 12, 12.
- Die 2 (4 faces, each equally likely): 1, 1, 6, 7.
game.contract: The contract settles at the sum of all the dice.

info.raw:
Fair value is 13 (die 1 mean 9.25 plus die 2 mean 3.75), and the sum's distribution is symmetric about 13: 7, 8, 12, 13, 14, 18, 19. No trade at 8/18 leaves it symmetric, so the fair value is still 13.

With alpha unknown (averaging about 0.48), I compared ask levels by expected profit per quote, with the bid side mirroring:

| Ask | Expected profit |
|---|---|
| 15 | about -0.06 |
| 16 | about +0.05 |
| 17 | about +0.10 |
| 18 | about +0.14 |
| 19 | about +0.11 |

An ask of 18 is best: only an informed trader holding 19 picks me off, for a loss of 1, while noise traders pay 5 over fair. So I keep 8 / 18.

{"bid": 8, "ask": 18}

Die 2 = 6, so settlement is 12, 13 or 18 (probabilities 1/4, 1/4, 1/2), giving a fair value of 15.25. The first two quotes carry no information, since none of these values would have traded at 8/18.

- **Ask 18:** an informed trader never buys here (18 is not above 18), and a noise trader buys about 20% of the time at 2.75 of edge. Lowering the ask exposes me to the 50% chance the value is 18, which costs more than the extra noise flow earns.
- **Bid 12:** an informed trader never sells here, and a noise trader sells about 16% of the time at 3.25 of edge. Raising the bid to 13 adds only a little noise profit while losing 1 to an informed seller when the value is 12, which is not worth it at the average alpha.

{"bid": 12, "ask": 18}

With die 2 = 6, the contract settles at 12, 13 or 18 (probabilities 1/4, 1/4, 1/2), so the fair value is 15.25.

- **Ask 18:** an informed trader buys only if the value is above the ask, which cannot happen at 18, so there is no adverse selection. A noise trader buys about 20% of the time, and I earn 2.75 of edge on each such sale. Any lower ask loses to an informed buyer when the value is 18, which costs more than the extra noise flow gains.
- **Bid 12:** an informed trader sells only if the value is below the bid, which cannot happen at 12. A noise trader sells about 16% of the time, and I earn 3.25 of edge on each such purchase. Raising the bid to 12.1 or higher exposes me to informed selling when the value is 12, and the three no-trades so far tilt the odds towards a high share of informed traders (expected alpha about 0.57), so that costs more than it gains.

{"bid": 12, "ask": 18}

**Fair value:** the sum has mean 13 (die 1 mean 9.25, die 2 mean 3.75), with possible values 7, 8, 12, 13, 14, 18, 19, symmetric about 13.

**Informed share:** four quotes with no trade in round 1 shift the posterior towards a high informed share, roughly 0.18 / 0.32 / 0.50 on alpha = 0.05 / 0.5 / 0.9, so the expected alpha is about 0.62.

**Quote choice:** at that alpha, any ask below 18 loses more to informed traders than it earns from noise traders. Expected profit per quote on the ask side:

| Ask | Expected profit |
|---|---|
| 16 | about −0.18 |
| 18 | about +0.05 |
| 19 | about +0.08 |
| 19.5 | about +0.06 |

An ask of 19 is the best: no informed trader can ever buy there, since the maximum settlement is 19, so only noise traders trade. By symmetry the best bid is 7, the minimum settlement.

{"bid": 7, "ask": 19}

With die 2 = 6, the contract settles at 12, 13 or 18 (probabilities 1/4, 1/4, 1/2), so fair value is 15.25.

- **Ask 18:** no informed trader ever buys here, since the value never exceeds 18. A noise trader buys about 20% of the time, giving me an edge of 2.75 per sale.
- **Bid 12:** no informed trader ever sells here, since the value is never below 12. A noise trader sells about 16% of the time, giving me an edge of 3.25 per purchase.

Tightening either side would add almost nothing from noise traders while opening me to informed losses, and the run of no-trades so far makes a high alpha more likely (my estimate averages about 0.63). I am keeping the quotes at the edges of the value range.

{"bid": 12, "ask": 18}

Die 2 = 6, so settlement is 12, 13 or 18 (probabilities 1/4, 1/4, 1/2), giving a fair value of 15.25.

Seven straight no-trades at wide quotes point towards a high informed share: my rough posterior on alpha is about 13% / 30% / 57% for 0.05 / 0.5 / 0.9, mean near 0.67.

- **Ask 18:** an informed trader never buys at 18, since no value exceeds it, while a noise trader who does buy pays 2.75 over fair. Going lower would hand an informed buyer a loss whenever the value is 18.
- **Bid 12:** an informed trader never sells at 12, and a noise seller gives me 3.25 of edge. Raising the bid to 13 gains a little from noise but loses to informed sellers when the value is 12, which is a net loss at this alpha estimate.

{"bid": 12, "ask": 18}

Fair value before any reveal is 13 (die 1 mean 9.25 + die 2 mean 3.75), with possible sums 7, 8, 12, 13, 14, 18, 19.

Eight quotes without a trade shift the odds towards a high share of informed traders: roughly 9% / 28% / 63% for alpha = 0.05 / 0.5 / 0.9, so about 0.71 on average.

At that level, any ask below 19 or bid above 7 loses more to informed traders than it earns from noise traders:

| Ask (bid is symmetric) | Expected profit per quote |
|---|---|
| 14 (bid 12) | about -0.69 |
| 18 (bid 8) | about +0.005 |
| 19 (bid 7) | about +0.06 |

Quoting at the extremes of the range means an informed trader can never profit against me, while I still collect about 6 per trade from the occasional noise trader.

- **Ask 19:** an informed trader never buys here, since the value is never above 19. Noise traders buy about 20% of the time, at an edge of 2.75.
- **Bid 13:** an informed trader never sells here, since the value is never below 13. Noise traders sell about 16% of the time, at an edge of 3.25.

Tightening either side inside the 13–19 range lets informed traders pick me off. Ten quotes without a trade put most of the weight on a high informed share (roughly 0.73 on average), so that is not worth it.

- **Informed risk:** a bid at 13 and an ask at 19 can never be hit by an informed trader, since no settlement value is below 13 or above 19.
- **Alpha estimate:** eleven straight no-trades point towards a high alpha (roughly 70% on 0.9 by my approximate update), so moving inside those bounds is costly.
- **Ask:** 19 sits 2.75 above fair, close to the profit-maximising distance against noise traders (about 2.5), and any lower ask loses to an informed buyer half the time.
- **Bid:** raising it above 13 adds only a sliver of noise-trader edge while exposing a quarter-probability informed loss, so 13 is best.

With that much informed flow, any quote inside the 7–19 range loses more to informed traders than it earns from noise traders. For example, an ask of 18 has expected profit of about -0.02 against about +0.05 at 19.

So I quote at the extremes of the range, where an informed trader can never profit and only noise traders can trade.

Fair value is 13 (die 1 mean 9.25 + die 2 mean 3.75), and the settlement can only be 7, 8, 12, 13, 14, 18 or 19.

- **Why 7 / 19:** an informed trader never sells at 7 or buys at 19, because the value is never below 7 or above 19. So these quotes only ever trade with noise traders, at a 6-point edge each time.
- **Why not tighter:** my estimate of alpha after the session so far is roughly 19% / 49% / 33% for 0.05 / 0.5 / 0.9, a mean near 0.55. At that level, 8 / 18 earns slightly less per side (about 0.08 against 0.09), and anything inside that loses to informed traders on the 18–19 and 7–8 outcomes.
- **Last trade:** the sale at 7 must have come from a noise trader, so it says nothing about the value, and the long position bought at 7 cannot lose.

{"bid": 7, "ask": 19}

Die 2 = 1, so the contract settles at 7, 8 or 13 (probabilities 1/4, 1/4, 1/2), giving a fair value of 10.25.

The sale at 7 in quote 1 must have come from a noise trader, since no settlement value is below 7. So it tells me nothing about die 1. The quiet history does shift the odds on alpha towards the higher values (roughly 0.18 / 0.49 / 0.33 for 0.05 / 0.5 / 0.9, a mean near 0.55).

With that much informed flow, I want quotes that an informed trader can never hit:

- **Ask 13:** no settlement value is above 13, so only noise traders buy (about 20% of them, at an edge of 2.75). Dropping the ask to 12 or 12.75 lets informed traders pick me off whenever die 1 is 12, which costs more than the extra noise flow earns.
- **Bid 7:** no settlement value is below 7, so only noise traders sell (about 16% of them, at an edge of 3.25). Raising the bid to 8 gains a little noise flow but loses 1 to informed traders whenever the value is 7, which is worse on balance.

Being long 1 does not change this, as there is no penalty for holding inventory to settlement.

{"bid": 7, "ask": 13}

Die 2 = 1, so the settlement is 7, 8 or 13 with probabilities 1/4, 1/4, 1/2, giving a fair value of 10.25.

- **Ask 13:** an informed trader never buys here, since the value cannot exceed 13. A noise trader buys about 20% of the time, and I make 2.75 on average per sale. Lowering the ask adds almost nothing from noise traders but starts losing to informed buyers when the value is 13.
- **Bid 7:** an informed trader never sells here, since the value cannot be below 7. A noise trader sells about 16% of the time, and I make 3.25 on average per purchase. Raising the bid towards 8 gains slightly from noise traders but loses more to informed sellers when the value is 7. My rough estimate of the informed share is about 37% on average, which is high enough that the trade-off does not pay.

Both trades so far this round were necessarily from noise traders, so they tell me nothing about the value.

{"bid": 7, "ask": 13}

Fair value before any reveal is 13 (die 1 mean 9.25 plus die 2 mean 3.75), with possible sums 7, 8, 12, 13, 14, 18 and 19.

No trade so far can have come from an informed counterparty, because my quotes sat at or beyond the extremes of the possible values. That makes the two trades in round 4 noise trades and gives a posterior on alpha of roughly 0.33 / 0.58 / 0.09 for 0.05 / 0.5 / 0.9, a mean of about 0.39.

Expected profit per quote on the ask side at that mean alpha (the bid side is essentially the mirror image):

| Ask | Noise gain | Informed loss | Net |
|---|---|---|---|
| 14 | 0.23 | 0.44 | −0.21 |
| 16 | 0.33 | 0.24 | 0.09 |
| 17 | 0.28 | 0.15 | 0.13 |
| 18 | 0.20 | 0.05 | 0.15 |
| 19 | 0.13 | 0.00 | 0.13 |

An ask of 18 is best: only a settlement of 19 can pick me off, for a loss of 1. A bid of 8 is the matching choice, exposed only to a settlement of 7.

{"bid": 8, "ask": 18}

Fair value before any reveal is 13 (die 1 mean 9.25 plus die 2 mean 3.75), and the distribution of the sum is symmetric around 13, so the no-trade on quote 1 leaves it at 13.

From the session so far, my posterior on alpha is roughly 0.34 / 0.57 / 0.09 for 0.05 / 0.5 / 0.9, a mean near 0.38. The two trades in round 4 were both against the settlement direction, so they came from noise traders, which makes 0.9 unlikely.

Comparing asks by expected profit this quote (the bid side mirrors it):

| Ask | Noise edge | Informed loss | Net |
|---|---|---|---|
| 16 | 0.338 | 0.179 | 0.159 |
| 17 | 0.280 | 0.101 | 0.179 |
| 18 | 0.202 | 0.022 | 0.179 |
| 19 | 0.128 | 0 | 0.128 |

17 and 18 are effectively tied, and I take 18 because an informed trader only hits it when the sum is 19, so the adverse-selection loss is smallest. The bid at 8 is the symmetric choice.

With die 2 = 1, the settlement can only be 7, 8 or 13 (prior fair value 10.25; about 10.8 after allowing for no informed seller hitting my 8 bid earlier this round).

- **Ask 13.2:** an informed trader never buys at 13 or above, so any ask from 13 up only trades with noise traders. Slightly above 13 gives the best balance of edge and fill probability.
- **Bid 8:** an informed trader only sells here if the value is 7, which is now unlikely and costs just 1. That small risk is outweighed by the extra noise-trader fills compared with bidding 7. Anything above 8 would also be hit when the value is 8, which is not worth it.

At that alpha, tight quotes lose more to informed traders than they earn from noise traders. An ask of 16 is slightly negative and 17 earns about 0.05. Asks of 18 and 19 both earn about 0.105, and 19 cannot be picked off by any settlement value. The bid side is symmetric, so I quote the extremes.

{"bid": 7, "ask": 19}

- **Ask 18:** an informed trader only buys if the value is strictly above the ask, so at 18 they never trade against me. This is also close to the best distance for noise traders (about 20% chance of a sale at an edge of 2.75).
- **Bid 12:** likewise no informed trader sells at 12, and noise traders sell about 16% of the time at an edge of 3.25. Raising the bid to 12.1 or 13 gains slightly more noise flow but lets informed traders sell to me when the value is 12; with my estimate of alpha at roughly 0.5 from the session history, that costs more than it earns.

game.title: Dice sum
game.description:
Four dice are rolled independently. Repeated numbers are separate faces.
- Die 1 (6 faces, each equally likely): 1, 1, 3, 4, 5, 8.
- Die 2 (8 faces, each equally likely): 0, 2, 3, 3, 5, 5, 10, 11.
- Die 3 (8 faces, each equally likely): 1, 1, 2, 3, 7, 8, 9, 12.
- Die 4 (6 faces, each equally likely): 0, 1, 3, 5, 9, 10.
game.contract: The contract settles at the sum of all the dice.

info.raw:
Fair value before any reveal is the sum of the die means: 3.667 + 4.875 + 5.375 + 4.667 ≈ 18.58, with a standard deviation of about 6.9.

Averaging over the three possible alpha values (mean about 0.48), I estimated the expected profit per quote at several half-spreads, using a normal approximation for the settlement value:

| Half-spread | Expected profit per quote |
|---|---|
| 6 | ≈ 0.24 |
| 7 | ≈ 0.30 |
| 8 | ≈ 0.31 |
| 9 | ≈ 0.29 |
| 10 | ≈ 0.24 |

The optimum is flat between 7 and 8, so I take 7, the tighter end, since more trades reveal more about alpha early in the session.

{"bid": 11.6, "ask": 25.6}

Fair value before any trade is about 18.6 (standard deviation about 6.9). The sale at 11.6 is roughly as likely to be informed as noise, so the public fair value drops to about 13, with a real chance that the sum is 11 or lower.

- **Bid:** I move it well below the last one, to 7.4, so an informed seller only hits it on very low sums while noise sellers still give a good edge.
- **Ask:** I keep it wide at 22. An informed buyer can only exist if the first sale was noise, which makes the ask roughly break-even across 20 to 23.

These figures come from normal-approximation estimates of the dice sum, not an exact enumeration.

{"bid": 7.4, "ask": 22.0}

Rough posterior after die 1 = 1 and the earlier sale at 11.6: fair value is about 11.6, with most of the weight on a sum of 8–11 and a high chance that informed traders are common. I'm quoting wide on both sides: a bid of 7.0 only loses to an informed seller when the sum is 6 or less, and an ask of 18.0 keeps the informed loss on high sums small while still earning from noise buyers.

{"bid": 7.0, "ask": 18.0}

Fair value now is about 11.1 by my estimate: die 1 = 1 plus 14.9 for the hidden dice gives 15.9, pulled down by the sale at 11.6 and the two no-trades, which point to a likely informed seller with the sum in the 8–11 range.

- **Bid 7.0:** a bid at 8 or above gets hit by an informed seller whenever the sum is below it, and the 8–11 range carries most of the informed weight. At 7.0 only sums of 6 or less cost me, while noise sellers are still profitable.
- **Ask 18.0:** expected profit is nearly flat between 17 and 18; at 18.0 an informed buyer only lifts me on sums of 19 or more, which are now unlikely.

{"bid": 7.0, "ask": 18.0}

Fair value before any reveal is 18.58 (die means 3.67 + 4.88 + 5.38 + 4.67), with a settlement standard deviation of about 6.9.

Round 1 shifts my view of alpha: the sale at 7 when settlement was 11 must have been a noise trader, while the first sale at 11.6 fits an informed one. My rough posterior is about 21% / 55% / 24% on 0.05 / 0.5 / 0.9, which behaves like alpha ≈ 0.5.

At that level, a half-spread of roughly 8 maximises expected profit per side: noise traders pay enough edge to cover losses to informed ones. The dice are skewed to the high side, so I set the ask slightly wider than the bid.

{"bid": 10.9, "ask": 27}

Fair value with nothing revealed is about 18.6 (dice means 3.67 + 4.88 + 5.38 + 4.67), with a standard deviation near 6.9. Round 1 leaves my estimate of alpha centred near 0.5, since the last sale at 7 against a settlement of 11 must have been a noise trader. At that level a normal approximation puts the best quote about 8 either side of fair. I shade both prices slightly upward because the sum is right-skewed.

With die 1 = 4 the unconditional fair value is about 18.9, but the sale at 11.3 last quote shifts weight towards a settlement at or below 11. My rough posterior puts the fair value near 15.6.

- **Bid 10.5:** staying below 11 means an informed seller only hits me when the settlement is 10 or less, while noise sellers still give me a large edge.
- **Ask 22.9:** this keeps a wide margin over noise buyers and limits losses to informed buyers to settlements of 23 or more.

At that alpha, the edge that best trades noise-trader profit against informed losses is roughly 6 to 6.5 from fair value. The sum is slightly right-skewed, so I set the ask a little wider than the bid.

game.description:
Three dice are rolled independently. Repeated numbers are separate faces.
- Die 1 (8 faces, each equally likely): 2, 5, 6, 6, 9, 10, 10, 11.
- Die 2 (6 faces, each equally likely): 0, 3, 5, 5, 9, 10.
- Die 3 (8 faces, each equally likely): 1, 2, 4, 6, 9, 10, 11, 12.
game.contract: The contract settles at the largest minus the smallest of the dice.

Before any reveal the fair value is 4 (the red count is uniform on 0 to 8). Averaging over the three possible alpha values, quotes near fair lose more to informed traders than they earn from noise traders. An ask of 7.0 and a bid of 1.0 give the best expected profit of the levels I checked, about 0.08 per side. At those prices an informed trader only trades when the urn is 8 or 0, so I lose at most 1 to them.

{"bid": 1.0, "ask": 7.0}

Before any reveal the fair value is 4 (uniform on 0–8), and the no-trade at 1/7 leaves it there by symmetry. With alpha unknown (mean about 0.48), I compared symmetric quotes by expected profit per side: noise-trader edge minus losses to informed traders.

| Ask (bid mirrored) | Expected profit per side |
|---|---|
| 5 | negative |
| 6 | about 0.03 |
| 6.5 | about 0.06 |
| 7 | about 0.08 |
| 7.2 | about 0.08 |
| 7.5 | about 0.075 |
| 7.9 | about 0.07 |

An ask of 7 (bid of 1) is about the best: only a settlement of exactly 8 or 0 can hurt me, while noise traders still pay 3 of edge when they trade. I am keeping the same quote.

{"bid": 1, "ask": 7}

**Fair value.** After a red first draw, the posterior on the number of red balls is proportional to R, giving a mean of 5.67. The two no-trades at 1/7 also make R = 8 less likely (an informed trader would have bought at 7), which pulls my estimate down to about 5.25.

**Ask.** Against an average informed share near 0.5, an ask of 7 only loses to informed traders when R = 8, and earns about 1.75 from noise buyers. Expected edge is roughly +0.17, and asks at 6 to 6.5 are worse because R = 7 is the most likely value.

**Bid.** A bid of 3 loses only when R is 1 or 2 and earns about 2.25 from noise sellers, for roughly +0.10. A bid of 4 is about break-even and 5 loses money.

{"bid": 3, "ask": 7}

Posterior after draw 1 = red, two no-trades at 1/7 and a buy at 7: P(8 red) is about 0.23 and fair value is about 5.7. Roughly 27% of the weight is on an informed counterparty.

- **Ask 8.0:** an informed buyer only lifts an ask below 8, so at 8.0 there is no adverse selection and I still earn about 2.3 per noise buyer. Expected profit is about 0.245, essentially the same as 7.8–7.9.
- **Bid 3.7:** this balances noise sellers (edge about 2.0) against informed sellers when there are 1–3 red. Expected profit is about 0.205, slightly better than 3.5 or 4.0.

{"bid": 3.7, "ask": 8.0}

**Reasoning**

- Round 1 settled at 4, so both buys there (at 7 and 8) must have come from noise traders, which points strongly to a low alpha. My posterior is roughly 0.72 / 0.26 / 0.01 on alpha = 0.05 / 0.5 / 0.9, giving an expected alpha of about 0.18.
- The buy at 6 this round has about a 20% chance of being informed (value 7 or 8), which lifts the fair value from 4 to about 4.7 and puts roughly 0.19 each on 7 and 8.
- Ask: expected profit per quote is about 0.19 at 6, 0.24 at 6.5, 0.25 at 7 and 0.18 at 8, so 7 is best. It earns 2.3 from noise buyers and only loses to an informed buyer when the value is 8.
- Bid: expected profit is about 0.20 at 2, 0.22 at 2.7–2.8, 0.21 at 3 and 0.16 at 3.5, so I bid 2.7.

{"bid": 2.7, "ask": 7}

Given draw 1 = red, the posterior on the red count is proportional to R (mean about 5.67). The earlier buy at 6 and the no-trade at 2.7/7 shift weight toward 7 and 8, so my fair value is about 6.1.

Round 1 settled at 4 after two buys at 7 and 8, so those were noise trades. That makes a low alpha most likely (roughly 67% for 0.05, 31% for 0.5, 2% for 0.9).

- **Ask 8:** an informed trader never buys at 8, since the value cannot exceed 8, so this side only sells to noise traders at about 1.9 above fair value.
- **Bid 4.4:** this buys from noise traders about 1.7 below fair value, and an informed trader only hits it when the count is 4 or lower, which is now unlikely.

{"bid": 4.4, "ask": 8}

Posterior after the red draw and this round's trades (a buy at 6, then a sell at 4.4) puts fair value near 5.7, with most weight on a low informed share but meaningful mass on 7 and 8 reds.

With position flat on the last quote, I quote for the widest edge against noise traders while limiting what an informed trader can take:

- **Ask 7.8:** only an 8-red urn can pick me off, and for just 0.2; expected profit is about 0.30, nearly flat anywhere from 7.5 to 8.
- **Bid 4.0:** an informed trader sells only at 3 reds or fewer; expected profit is about 0.27, better than 3.5 or 4.5.

{"bid": 4.0, "ask": 7.8}

**Reading the session so far:** five of the earlier trades and non-trades could only have come from noise traders (for example, buys at 7 and 8 when the contract settled at 4, and no sale at my 2.7 and 4 bids when it settled at 2). That puts roughly 0.89 probability on alpha = 0.05, 0.11 on alpha = 0.5, and almost none on 0.9, so an effective alpha of about 0.1.

**Fair value now:** the buy at 5.8 shifts the urn's expected red count up only slightly, from 4 to about 4.4, because the buyer was most likely noise.

**Quote:** against mostly noise traders with standard deviation 2.2, the profit-maximising edge is about 1.8 each side of fair value, slightly wider than the pure-noise optimum to cover the small informed risk. My short position of 1 is far from the limit, so I do not skew for inventory.

{"bid": 2.6, "ask": 6.2}

**Fair value.** After a red first draw the posterior on the number of red balls is proportional to R, giving a mean of about 5.67. The earlier buy at 5.8 and the no-trade at 2.6 / 6.2 shift it slightly up, to roughly 5.9.

**Informed share.** Rounds 1 and 2 contained five quotes where an informed trader would have acted differently given the settlement values (4 and 2). That makes alpha = 0.9 essentially impossible and puts roughly 88% on alpha = 0.05 and 12% on alpha = 0.5, so the effective informed share is about 10%.

**Quote.** Against noise with standard deviation 2.2, the profit-maximising distance from fair value is about 1.65, widened slightly for the informed share.

- **Ask 7.6:** an informed trader only buys if the urn holds 8 red, losing me 0.4, so the adverse-selection cost is small.
- **Bid 4.0:** an informed trader only sells if the urn holds 3 or fewer red, which is about 13% likely.

The position of -1 is far from the limit with two quotes left, so I am not skewing for inventory.

{"bid": 4.0, "ask": 7.6}

**Fair value.** After draw 1 = 0, the posterior on the red count is proportional to (8 − r), which gives a mean of about 2.33.

**How informed the flow is.** Across rounds 1–3 there were six quotes where an informed trader would have acted differently from what happened (for example, buying at 7 and 8 when the value was 4). That makes alpha = 0.9 essentially impossible and alpha = 0.05 roughly 93% likely, with the rest on 0.5. My effective alpha is about 0.08.

**Adjusting for this round's trades.** The buy at 5.8 and the earlier no-trade nudge the estimate up only slightly because the flow is mostly noise. My fair value is about 2.55.

**Quote width.** Against noise traders with standard deviation 2.2, the profit-maximising half-spread is about 0.75 standard deviations, or roughly 1.65. I widen the ask slightly because an informed buyer costs more there than an informed seller does at the bid. The position limit is not binding at −1.

{"bid": 0.9, "ask": 4.3}

Fair value this round is about 2.4: the blue draw alone gives a mean of 2.33, and the earlier buy at 5.8 and sell at 0.9 roughly offset.

The session history points strongly to a low informed share. At least six past trades or non-trades were impossible for an informed counterparty given the settlement, so alpha = 0.9 is effectively ruled out and alpha = 0.05 is much more likely than 0.5.

Against mostly noise traders (standard deviation 2.2), the profit-maximising edge is roughly 1.7–1.9 either side of fair value. I keep the bid below 1 so an informed seller only hits it when the urn has 0 red balls, and I set the ask a little wide because an informed buyer at 5–7 red balls costs more.

{"bid": 0.6, "ask": 4.2}

Fair value is still 4 (no reveal yet, and the symmetric no-trade at 2/6 does not move it).

From the history, at least seven counterparties traded or stood aside in ways an informed trader could not have, which all but rules out alpha = 0.9. The remaining evidence leaves 0.05 and 0.5 about equally likely, so I use an effective alpha of roughly 0.28.

At that alpha, the expected profit per side is nearly flat for an ask between 6.0 and 6.5 (about 0.17 per quote), peaking near 6.2. The bid is symmetric at 1.8.

{"bid": 1.8, "ask": 6.2}

**Fair value.** After draw 1 = 0 the posterior on red count is proportional to (8 − r), giving a mean of 2.33. The two no-trades at 2/6 and 1.8/6.2 make the extremes (0, 1, 7, 8) less likely, since an informed trader would have hit those quotes, which lifts my estimate to about 2.7.

**Alpha.** At least 7 of the 16 earlier quotes were clearly noise (trades or no-trades an informed trader would not have made), which all but rules out alpha = 0.9. I put roughly 60–65% on 0.05 and the rest on 0.5, so an effective alpha near 0.2–0.25.

**Quotes.** Against noise with standard deviation 2.2, the best edge is about 1.7 either side of fair. A bid of 1.0 is only picked off by an informed trader when the count is 0. An ask of 4.6 is only picked off at 5 or more, which is fairly unlikely here. Expected profit is about 0.24 per side, and asks anywhere from 4.5 to 5 score about the same.

{"bid": 1.0, "ask": 4.6}

Fair value after a blue first draw is about 2.3, and the three no-trades this round nudge it to roughly 2.6. The history shows many trades that an informed counterparty would never have made, so alpha is very likely 0.05 or 0.5, not 0.9. With adverse selection that light, I quote wide around 2.6 to earn from noise traders: a bid of 1.0 (only a settlement of 0 hurts) and an ask of 4.5.

{"bid": 1.0, "ask": 4.5}

Reading the history, seven trades or non-trades were impossible for an informed counterparty (e.g. buying at 7 and 8 when the value was 4, not selling at 2.7 when it was 2), which all but rules out alpha = 0.9. Weighing the remaining evidence gives roughly 70% on alpha = 0.5 and 30% on alpha = 0.05, so an expected alpha of about 0.37.

With nothing revealed, the fair value is 4 and the value is uniform on 0 to 8. At that alpha, the expected profit per side peaks at about 3 away from fair:

| Ask | Expected profit |
|---|---|
| 6.0 | 0.109 |
| 6.5 | 0.122 |
| 7.0 | 0.124 |
| 7.5 | 0.104 |
| 8.0 | 0.088 |

At 7 only a value of 8 can pick me off on the ask, and by symmetry only a value of 0 on the bid at 1.

{"bid": 1, "ask": 7}

**Reading alpha from the history.** Seven trades or non-trades so far are impossible for an informed counterparty (for example, buying at 7 and 8 in round 1 when the value was 4, or selling at 0.9 in round 4 when it was 6). That all but rules out alpha = 0.9. Weighing the remaining ambiguous events, I put roughly 70% on alpha = 0.5 and 30% on alpha = 0.05, so the expected share of informed traders is about 0.37.

**Pricing this quote.** Fair value is still 4 by symmetry. The no-trade at 1/7 last quote makes the extremes 0 and 8 somewhat less likely, which reduces the cost of being picked off. Expected profit per side at a few ask levels (bid mirrored around 4):

| Ask | Expected profit |
|---|---|
| 6.0 | about 0.134 |
| 6.5 | about 0.141 |
| 7.0 | about 0.138 |

The optimum is flat around 6.5, so I quote symmetrically at 1.5 / 6.5.

{"bid": 1.5, "ask": 6.5}

After a blue first draw, the value's posterior mean is about 2.33 on the draw alone. The two no-trades in stage 1 make extreme values less likely, so I put the public fair value near 2.7.

From the history, alpha = 0.9 is effectively ruled out: several trades and no-trades could only have come from noise traders. That leaves 0.05 and 0.5 roughly equally likely.

Averaging expected profit over those two cases, the best quotes sit on integers, because an informed trader only trades when the value is strictly beyond the price:

- **Ask 5:** expected profit is about 0.22, essentially flat between 4.5 and 5. At exactly 5, an informed trader with value 5 does not buy.
- **Bid 1:** expected profit is about 0.24, slightly better than 0.5 and clearly better than 1.5. At exactly 1, an informed trader with value 1 does not sell.

{"bid": 1.0, "ask": 5.0}

**Fair value:** after draw 1 = 0 the prior mean is 2.33, but three no-trade quotes this round make the extremes (0, and 6 or more) less likely if informed traders are common, which pulls my estimate up to about 2.8.

**Alpha:** earlier rounds show seven quotes that an informed trader could not have produced (for example buying at 7 and 8 when the value was 4), so alpha = 0.9 is effectively ruled out. I put roughly two-thirds on 0.5 and one-third on 0.05.

**Quote choice:** bids and asks on integers are best, because an informed trader only trades when the value is strictly beyond the price. Approximate expected profit per side:

| Ask | Expected profit | | Bid | Expected profit |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| 4 | 0.16 | | 0.5 | 0.20 |
| 4.5 | 0.21 | | 1 | 0.22 |
| 5 | 0.22 | | 1.5 | 0.17 |
| 5.5 | 0.19 | | 2 | 0.09 |
| 6 | 0.15 | | | |

An ask of 5 loses only to values of 6 or 7, and a bid of 1 loses only to a value of 0, while both still catch a fair share of noise traders.

{"bid": 1, "ask": 5}

game.title: Urn of unknown mix
game.description: An urn holds 11 balls, each red or blue. Each ball was independently painted red with probability 0.3. 2 balls are drawn without replacement. Revealed draws show 1 for red and 0 for blue.
game.contract: The contract settles at 10 times the number of red balls originally in the urn.

info.raw:
Prior: reds ~ Binomial(11, 0.3), so fair value is 33 with settlement values on multiples of 10.

I compared candidate quotes using the average alpha (about 0.48), weighing expected gain from noise traders against expected loss to informed traders:

| Quote | Noise gain | Informed loss | Net expected profit |
|---|---|---|---|
| Ask 45 | 2.14 | 2.10 | 0.09 |
| Ask 50 | 1.62 | 1.05 | 0.33 |
| Ask 60 | 0.51 | 0.27 | 0.14 |
| Bid 25 | 2.15 | 2.89 | -0.28 |
| Bid 20 | 2.06 | 1.33 | 0.43 |
| Bid 10 | 0.88 | 0.20 | 0.36 |

Quoting exactly on the settlement grid helps: an informed trader with value 50 does not lift an ask of 50, and one with value 20 does not hit a bid of 20.

{"bid": 20, "ask": 50}

Prior value is 10 × Binomial(11, 0.3), so fair value is about 33 with settlement only on multiples of 10. After a no-trade at 20/50 the fair value barely moves (roughly 33.4), and alpha is still essentially unknown.

Comparing candidate prices on each side (averaging over the three alpha values):

- **Ask 50:** noise traders pay about 16.6 over fair, while informed traders only hit it when the value is 60 or more, which is unlikely. This beats 40 and 45, where an informed buyer at value 50 costs too much.
- **Bid 20:** noise traders sell about 13.4 under fair, and informed traders only sell when the value is 0 or 10. This beats 25 and 30, where the value-20 case (about a quarter of the mass) is picked off.

Quoting exactly on the multiples of 10 matters: an informed trader with value 50 or 20 does not trade at those prices.

{"bid": 20, "ask": 50}

Fair value after the red draw is about 38 (40 from the draw alone, pulled down slightly because nobody traded against 20/50 in stage 1, which makes extreme values less likely).

Settlement can only be a multiple of 10, so I set quotes exactly on those points where an informed trader has no edge:

- **Ask 50:** an informed buyer only trades if the value is 60 or more, which is now unlikely (about 5%), while noise buyers pay roughly 12 over fair.
- **Bid 20:** an informed seller only trades if the value is 10 (about 1%), while noise sellers give up roughly 18 under fair.

Tighter quotes (bid 30 or ask 40.1) would hand the informed trader the likely 20 or 50 outcomes and come out worse on my estimate.

{"bid": 20, "ask": 50}

**Reasoning:** The prior value is 10 × Binomial(11, 0.3), mean 33. Five quotes at 20/50 with no trade shift belief towards high alpha (roughly 0.17 / 0.31 / 0.52 on 0.05 / 0.5 / 0.9), so adverse selection is the main risk.

Expected profit per quote under that belief, by price level:

| Side | Price | Expected profit |
|---|---|---|
| Bid | 20 | about -0.08 |
| Bid | 15 | about +0.07 |
| Bid | 10 | about +0.20 |
| Bid | 0 | about +0.07 |
| Ask | 50 | about -0.06 |
| Ask | 60 | about +0.02 |
| Ask | 70 | about 0 |

A bid of 10 only loses to an informed seller when the urn has zero reds, and an ask of 60 only loses when there are seven or more, so both sides stay slightly positive even if alpha is high.

{"bid": 10, "ask": 60}

Fair value is about 32: after a blue first draw the remaining 10 balls average 3 red (30), and three no-trades at wide quotes make the tails (≤10 or ≥60) unlikely and nudge the estimate up slightly.

The no-trades so far also favour a high informed share (my rough posterior puts alpha near 0.65 on average). So I keep the quotes at levels an informed trader only hits in the tails:

- **Ask 50:** an informed buyer only trades if the value is 60 or more, which is now very unlikely. Tightening to the low 40s would hand the informed trader the value-50 case and comes out worse.
- **Bid 20:** an informed seller only trades if the value is 10 or less. Raising the bid above 20 would lose to the informed trader at value 20, which outweighs the extra noise flow.

Both sides earn a positive expected edge from noise traders (roughly 0.5 on the ask and 0.6 on the bid).

{"bid": 20, "ask": 50}

Prior value is 33 (red count is Binomial(11, 0.3)), settling on multiples of 10.

Eight quotes with no trade, where both settlements were 50 so an informed trader could never have traded, shift my belief on alpha to roughly 10% / 28% / 62% for 0.05 / 0.5 / 0.9. A high informed share is now the most likely case, so I am quoting defensively.

- **Bid 10:** an informed trader only sells here if the urn has zero reds (about 2%), while noise sellers still hit it about 4% of the time at a 23-point edge. Expected profit is about +0.12 per quote.
- **Ask 60:** an informed trader only buys if there are 7 or more reds (about 2%). This is roughly break-even (about −0.03), and I keep it because any trade there helps identify alpha after settlement.

Tighter quotes such as 20/50 would lose about 0.57 per quote in expectation under my current belief, so I am not paying that to learn alpha faster.

{"bid": 10, "ask": 60}

Draw 1 was blue, so the other 10 balls are each red with probability 0.3: fair value is about 30.

Ten straight no-trades make a high informed share likely (roughly 63% on alpha = 0.9, 27% on 0.5, 9% on 0.05), so I keep quotes wide and on settlement grid points, where an informed trader at exactly that value does not trade.

- **Bid 10:** only a settlement of 0 hurts, and two earlier no-trades at a bid of 10 this round have largely ruled that out. Noise sellers still give about 20 of edge, so this is clearly positive.
- **Ask 50:** informed buyers only hit it at 60 or above, while noise buyers give about 20 of edge. It is roughly a tie with 60, marginally ahead on my estimate.

{"bid": 10, "ask": 50}

Fair value after a blue first draw is about 30 (10 remaining balls at 0.3 each), with settlement on multiples of 10.

Eleven quotes without a trade point to a high share of informed counterparties: my rough posterior puts about 0.63 on alpha = 0.9 and 0.27 on alpha = 0.5. So I quote exactly on the grid points where an informed trader gains nothing.

- **Ask 50:** an informed buyer only lifts it if settlement is 60 or more, which the no-trade at 10/50 last quote already makes unlikely. Noise buyers still pay about 20 over fair.
- **Bid 10:** an informed seller only hits it if settlement is 0, again unlikely. Noise sellers give up about 20 under fair.
- **Why not tighter:** moving either side inward to 20 or 40 exposes me to settlements of 10 or 50, each around 11–13% likely, and the expected loss to informed traders outweighs the extra noise flow.

{"bid": 10, "ask": 50}

**Reading the session so far:** twelve quotes with no trade is far more likely when most counterparties are informed, since each settlement of 50 meant an informed trader never crossed my quotes, while a noise trader would have traded fairly often. Weighing the three alpha values by how well they explain the silence gives roughly 8% for 0.05, 26% for 0.5 and 66% for 0.9, so expected alpha is about 0.73.

**Fair value:** with nothing revealed, the urn holds 11 × 0.3 = 3.3 red balls on average, so fair value is 33.

**Expected profit per quote at that posterior:**

| Side | Price | Expected profit |
|---|---|---|
| Bid | 20 | about -0.41 |
| Bid | 10 | about +0.09 |
| Bid | 0 | about +0.05 |
| Ask | 50 | about -0.33 |
| Ask | 60 | about -0.06 |
| Ask | 70 | about -0.01 |

A bid of 10 is the only quote with positive expectation: an informed trader sells there only when the urn has zero red balls (about 2%), while a noise trader who sells gives me 23 of edge. Every ask loses, because the upper tail of the settlement value is fat enough that informed buyers cost more than the rare noise buyer pays. I considered quoting tighter to learn alpha faster, but it costs about 0.7 per quote in expectation and the no-trade signal separates the cases slowly, so it is not worth it.

{"bid": 10, "ask": null}

**Reading the session so far.** Twelve quotes in rounds 1–3 drew no trades, although a noise trader would have hit those quotes roughly a quarter of the time. That points strongly to a high share of informed traders (roughly 75% weight on alpha = 0.9).

**Reading the sale at 10.** An informed trader sells at 10 only if the urn has zero red balls (about a 2% event). A noise trader sells there about 4% of the time, but noise traders are probably rare. Combining these, I put about two-thirds probability on the contract settling at 0, which drops fair value from 33 to roughly 11.

**Ask.** I checked asks at 20, 30, 40 and 50. In each case the expected loss to informed buyers, in the scenario where the value is not 0, outweighs the gain from noise buyers. I am not quoting an ask.

**Bid.** Any positive bid gets hit by informed sellers whenever the value is 0, which is now the likely case. A bid of exactly 0 cannot lose: an informed trader with value 0 does not sell at 0, and anything bought at 0 settles at 0 or more. Noise traders valuing it below 0 will still sell about 19% of the time, so it is a free option.

{"bid": 0, "ask": null}

Fair value after a blue first draw would normally be 30, but the sale at my bid of 10 changes that. Three rounds of wide quotes with no trades point to a high alpha, and an informed trader only sells at 10 if the urn has zero reds. I put roughly 65% on a settlement of 0, which makes the public fair value about 10–11.

- **Bid:** any bid above 0 gets hit by the informed trader when the value is 0, which is the likely case. A bid of 0 can only be hit by a noise trader with a negative valuation, and buying at 0 can never lose.
- **Ask:** if the value is 0, the informed trader never buys, so only the rare noise trader pays me. If the value is not 0, the informed trader buys only when the value is above my ask. Every ask level I checked (10, 20, 30) has negative expected profit, and at 50 or above almost nobody trades, so I leave the ask out.

{"bid": 0, "ask": null}

**Fair value now is about 10, not 30.** The sale at my bid of 10 in quote 1 is strong evidence of an informed seller who knows the urn has zero reds.

- **Alpha:** three rounds of wide quotes with no trades favour high alpha. After this round's sale and the blue draw, I put roughly 0.63 on alpha = 0.9, 0.28 on 0.5 and 0.09 on 0.05.
- **Settlement:** a noise trader sells at 10 only about 4% of the time when fair is 33, while an informed trader sells there only if the settlement is 0 (prior about 2%). Combined with the blue draw, that gives about a 68% chance the contract settles at 0, and otherwise an expected value of about 31.

**Ask: none.** Any ask from 30 to 60 loses more to informed buyers who know the value is above it than it earns from noise traders, so every ask I checked has negative expected profit.

**Bid: 0.** An informed trader with value 0 does not sell at a bid of 0, so the only sellers are noise traders, and buying from them at 0 is worth about +1.15 in expectation. Raising the bid even to 0.1 invites the informed zero-value seller and lowers the expected profit; a negative bid trades too rarely.

{"bid": 0, "ask": null}

Fair value before any reveal is 33 (11 balls × 0.3 × 10). The history (one trade in 16 quotes, and that one a sale at 10 when the value was 0) points strongly to a high informed share: roughly 81% weight on alpha = 0.9, 18% on 0.5, 1% on 0.05.

With that much informed flow, every ask I checked loses in expectation: the informed buy only when the value is above my ask, and noise buyers are too rare to pay for it. So I post no ask.

On the bid side, a bid of 10 is about break-even (loses to an informed seller when the value is 0, gains from rare noise sellers). A bid of 0 cannot lose, since the contract never settles below 0, and still picks up the occasional noise seller at a 33-point edge. That is the best expected profit of the bids I checked.

{"bid": 0, "ask": null}

Past trades point strongly to a high share of informed counterparties (posterior roughly 80% on alpha = 0.9), so any quote an informed trader could hit loses money on average.

- **Bid 0:** an informed trader never sells here, since the settlement value cannot be below 0, so the only fills are rare noise sellers at a price far below the fair value of 33. This is a small positive expectation with no adverse selection.
- **No ask:** at 50, 60, 70 and 80 the expected loss to informed buyers outweighs the gain from noise buyers, and above that noise fills are too rare to matter.

{"bid": 0, "ask": null}

Fair value after a blue first draw is 30 (the remaining 10 balls are each red with probability 0.3).

The session history (12 untraded wide quotes, then an immediate sale at 10 in a round that settled at 0) points strongly to a high informed share: roughly 81% on alpha = 0.9, 18% on 0.5 and 1% on 0.05.

- **Ask:** against that mix, every ask level loses in expectation (about -0.26 at 50, -0.05 at 60, slightly negative at 70), because informed buyers pick off the upper tail more than noise buyers pay. I leave the ask out.
- **Bid:** a bid at 0 can never be hit by an informed trader, since the settlement value cannot be below 0, so it only catches the occasional noise seller, at 30 below fair value. That is worth about +0.06 in expectation. Raising the bid to 2, 5 or 10 lowers the expected profit to about +0.03, +0.01 and -0.01.

{"bid": 0, "ask": null}

**Fair value:** with draw 1 blue, the other 10 balls are each red with probability 0.3, so the expected settlement is 30.

**Alpha:** the one trade so far was a sale at 10 in a round that settled at 0, and the many no-trades at wide quotes also fit informed counterparties. My rough posterior is about 0.81 on alpha = 0.9, 0.18 on 0.5 and 0.01 on 0.05, a mean near 0.82.

**Quotes at that alpha:**
- **Ask:** any ask from 40 to 80 loses on average, because informed buyers pick off the high settlements more than noise buyers pay. An ask of 100 can never be hit by an informed trader, so it is free.
- **Bid:** a bid of 0 can never be hit by an informed trader (settlement cannot be below 0), and a noise seller there gives me about 30 of edge. Expected profit is about +0.06, against roughly zero at a bid of 10.

{"bid": 0, "ask": 100}

**Reading the history:** almost every quote went untraded while the settlement sat inside my spread, and the one trade (round 4, sold to me at 10) came when the value was 0. That pattern is far more likely under a high informed share: my rough posterior is about 83% on alpha = 0.9, 16% on 0.5 and 1% on 0.05.

**Fair value:** with no draws revealed, the red count is Binomial(11, 0.3), so the fair value is 33 with a standard deviation of about 15.

**Ask side:** at an expected alpha near 0.83, every ask I checked loses money. At 50, 60 and 70, the expected loss to informed buyers is roughly three times the gain from noise buyers. An ask of 110 can never lose, since the value cannot exceed 110, so I post it as a harmless placeholder.

**Bid side:** a bid of 0 can never lose, because an informed trader only sells below 0 and the value is never negative. It still picks up the occasional noise seller at a 33-point edge, worth about +0.03 per quote. game.title: Dice sum
game.description:
Three dice are rolled independently. Repeated numbers are separate faces.
- Die 1 (8 faces, each equally likely): 1, 3, 3, 5, 5, 6, 6, 9.
- Die 2 (6 faces, each equally likely): 2, 3, 5, 8, 9, 11.
- Die 3 (4 faces, each equally likely): 0, 3, 3, 5.
game.contract: The contract settles at the sum of all the dice.

game.title: Dice/cards product
game.description:

- Die 1 (8 faces, each equally likely): 3, 3, 5, 7, 8, 9, 10, 12.

game.contract: The contract settles at the product of the dice.

info.raw:
Fair value before any reveal is 7.125 × 7.5 ≈ 53.4, but the 32 possible products range from 9 to 132 with a long right tail, and alpha averages about 0.48 across its three possible values.

- **Ask side:** any ask near fair value loses more to informed buyers than it earns from noise traders (at 72, roughly −1.6 per quote under the prior). An ask of 132 can never be hit by an informed trader, so it is free, with a tiny noise gain.
- **Bid side:** the left tail is short, so a low bid is profitable. The best myopic bid is around 18–21 (about +0.95 per quote); a bid of 30 earns about +0.5 but trades more often, which tells me more about alpha once the round settles.

I am taking the slightly more informative bid, because learning whether alpha is 0.05 is worth far more over the remaining 23 quotes than the 0.45 given up here.

{"bid": 30, "ask": 132}

**Fair value.** The unconditional mean is 7.125 × 7.5 ≈ 53.4. After quote 1 went untraded at 30/132, products below 30 are less likely (an informed trader would have sold), which lifts my estimate to about 59.

**Bid.** At 30, an informed seller only hits me on products below 30, which are now down-weighted. Noise sellers arrive about 11% of the time and give me roughly 29 of edge each. I estimate a net of about +1.3 per quote, and bids of 28, 31 and 33 all come out slightly worse.

**Ask.** With alpha unknown and averaging near 0.47, every ask from 80 to 121 loses more to informed buyers on the high products (up to 132) than it earns from noise. At 132 no informed trader can ever lift me, so it is a free, slightly positive quote.

I am keeping the same quote as last time.

Die 1 = 8, so the contract settles at 24, 48, 80 or 88 with equal probability, giving a fair value of 60.

- **Ask 88:** no informed trader can profit from buying at 88, since the highest settlement is 88. Noise traders still buy there about 12% of the time, paying 28 over fair value. Lower asks earn slightly more from noise traders but lose to informed buyers whenever die 2 is 11, which nets out worse at the average alpha of about 0.48.
- **Bid 24:** by the same logic, no informed trader sells at the lowest possible settlement. Noise traders sell there about 7% of the time, 36 under fair value. Raising the bid adds informed losses faster than noise gains.

game.description: An urn holds 6 balls, each red or blue. The number of red balls is equally likely to be any of 0, 1, ..., 6. 4 balls are drawn without replacement. Revealed draws show 1 for red and 0 for blue.
game.contract: The contract settles at 10 times the number of red balls originally in the urn.
